browser_date_fixture.cause: The real-date shared browser server correctly disabled catalogue rows outside their review window on 25 November. Four existing offline example and knowledge tests timed out waiting for Use v1.
browser_date_fixture.correction: Only the Playwright-launched shared server uses 1 November 2026 plus monotonic elapsed time. The canonical workspace entrypoint, root lock, security guards, lease progression, product facts and production freshness validation remain unchanged. Per-case isolated intake servers retain their existing clocks.

cli_review_fixture.cause: The old subprocess assigned c.build on a compatibility wrapper, which no longer owns the canonical CLI build hook. Its intended 26 October clock was not injected, and demo-review failed after evidence expired.
cli_review_fixture.correction: Set the intended process-local clock before importing the canonical CLI main. All restart, exact receipt, approval, revision, simulator and export assertions remain.

date_sensitive_fixture.cause: The subprocess inherited the real date while the rest of this fixture uses 26 October 2026. Bundled product evidence has review_by 24 November 2026, so the test began failing on 25 November.
date_sensitive_fixture.correction: Pin time.time in this test subprocess before imports capture its default, then invoke the canonical CLI main. Production evidence, expiry validation and provider-loading behavior are unchanged.

evidence_commit_contract: The final report and invariant ledger are a later evidence-only commit. Source attribution is per gate: backend partitions 1-3 began on d685514, partition 4 and boundaries bind the final source, and the interface began on c3db76b. Later changes repair native CLI and HTTP test fixtures only. The full affected HTTP class and all other users of its setup were rerun after its clock correction. Production, frontend and browser fixture launch/body code are unchanged across those later native fixture commits.

finding.cause: Every other cached record was demoted and the replayed receipt was prepended regardless of revision. Reconciling revision 1 therefore made revision 2 appear historical.
finding.correction: Merge and deduplicate by original request, order by immutable review revision, retain the newest server-reported projection and existing historical reasons, and update displayed selection with the same merged state. A known higher revision can only demote an older one; it cannot promote a cached record.
finding.title: Preserve the current review when reconciling older history

backend.attribution: These are the repository existing CI partitions. Independent unittest discovery and all four timing records establish exact coverage of all 1171 test IDs, with no missing or duplicate cases. After the shared HTTP fixture clock changed, its complete 19-case class and all other users were also rerun in the 40-case intake/admission check; the affected fourth partition was repeated. Earlier failed/interrupted attempts are not reported as passes.
backend.command: BACKEND_TIMINGS=/private/tmp/iwoca-preparation-history-backend-N.json make test-shard SHARD=N BACKEND_SHARDS=4 (N=1,2,3,4; partition 4 rerun after its fixture repair)

limits: Finite controlled response-order schedules do not establish every possible timing interleaving.
The exact cause of the prior reviewer run is not proven from its trace. These checks establish the newly reproduced races and corrected schedules, not absence of every possible intermittent failure.

No live provider conformance, deployment, schema change or paid model activation was performed for this frontend projection correction. Previous provider evidence retains its earlier source attribution.
The fresh make test gate includes native SQLite, restart, HTTP and Hrana-wire regressions.

observed: Newest revision 2 became historical after reconciling revision 1.
Retry was enabled while the initial store identity response was held.
A delayed empty history response removed the saved-review heading after confirmation.
before.production_bundle: The previously built original component bundle was used for the red checks; new regression tests were added before changing the production component.

native_oracles: The original immutable payload and expiry stay unchanged.
There are exactly two review rows after the competing review scenario, and replay sends no additional POST.
Model call and campaign approval tables remain empty.

related_recovery_corrections.cause: An in-flight history read captured before confirmation could arrive afterward with no records and erase the confirmed receipt.
related_recovery_corrections.correction: Abort obsolete read-only preview/history requests when a receipt is reconciled. Existing signal checks discard delayed completions.

related_recovery_corrections.cause: Recovery was enabled before the parent finished loading store identity. Completing that initialization during reconciliation changed the selection key and could discard the recovered view.
related_recovery_corrections.correction: Enable original-request recovery only after store identity is available. Exact store matching and original receipt verification are unchanged.

invariants: Reconciliation is not a new review and cannot demote a newer native review.
Late reads cannot erase a later confirmed receipt.
Startup identity changes cannot discard successfully reconciled recovery.
Original replay retains exact payload, expiry, scope and no-generation authority.

shared_http_fixture.cause: The audience test replaced workspace.real_clock after composition, leaving its audience application with the original real date. Dataset retrieval then correctly returned 409 for expired sources.
shared_http_fixture.correction: Inject a mutable fixture clock at workspace construction and advance the shared fixture value through the existing cases. Every clock consumer now sees the same intended historical time; production source and security/freshness assertions are unchanged.
